core_obligations: Construct L_H and the maximal open W of Hilb^g where it lands in F
Prove the claim: the zero scheme of the adjunction section is a relative effective Cartier divisor of degree g
Produce the inverse functor assignment via the divisor and conclude the isomorphism

difficulty_reason: Prove the open subfunctor F (invertible modules L with Rf_*L invertible in degree 0, adjusted at sigma) is representable by an open subscheme of Hilb^g_{X/k}: build L_H = O(D_univ) tensor pr_H^* sigma_H^* O(D_univ)^{-1} on H = Hilb^g, a point of Picardfunctor_{X/k,sigma}(H) defining h_H -> Picardfunctor; take the maximal open W where L_H lands in F (the open of perfect-lemma-open-where-cohomology-in-degree-i-rank-r-geometric for i=0, r=1); for L in F(T) with Rf_{T,*}L = N[0], show the zero scheme of the adjunction section s of L tensor f_T^*N^{-1} is a relative effective Cartier divisor of degree g (claim: reduce to fields by cohomology-and-base-change, compute deg = chi - chi(O) = g, nonzero section gives Cartier divisor); D defines m : T -> H pulling back D_univ, m factors through W, and adjusting at sigma identifies the functors.
